evals.prompt: I have test scores for students nested within schools and want to model the effect of study hours, allowing it to vary by school. What model and what should I report?
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-multilevel-models: fits a random-intercept-and-slope model (statsmodels MixedLM or R lmer with (1 + hours | school)), reports the ICC and variance components, and lists the full specification / estimation / assumptions / effect-size reporting items.

assertions.value: Specifies random intercept + slope by school and enforces the multilevel reporting checklist (variance components, estimation, assumptions).

evals.prompt: Repeated binary outcomes measured on the same patients over time — fit a multilevel logistic regression.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-multilevel-models: fits a GLMM (random intercept per patient) via statsmodels/bambi or R glmer(family=binomial), and reports the random-effects structure and estimation method.

assertions.value: Uses a generalized linear mixed model with a patient-level random effect for repeated binary measures.

evals.prompt: How much of the variation in employee satisfaction is between teams versus within teams?
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-multilevel-models: fits an intercept-only (null) model and reports the ICC as the between-team share of variance, noting whether multilevel structure is even warranted.

evals.prompt: Just run an ordinary least squares regression of price on square footage — no grouping.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger this skill; defers to alterlab-statsmodels. Single-level OLS with no nesting has no random-effects structure to model.

evals.prompt: I have panel data and want two-way fixed effects to identify the causal effect of a policy.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger this skill; defers to alterlab-causal-inference. Panel fixed effects for causal identification is a design/estimation problem, not variance-partitioning multilevel modeling.
